implementation_notes: encoding/json decodes into a statically chosen type, so the choice must already have been made by the caller, and encoding/gob goes the other way by writing its own type ids into the stream (the content-based sibling). The property-based realization is therefore a hand-written map[string]func([]byte) (T, error) keyed by a header value, with the header read before the payload reaches any decoder; kafka-go and sarama both expose record headers as a slice of {Key, Value []byte} pairs. Nothing in the standard library replaces the classic registry structure, so the missing-token policy is yours to write.
pitfalls: Header values are []byte and Kafka permits repeated keys; decide once whether the first or last wins, or clients will disagree.
A map lookup on a missing key returns the zero value without complaint - always check the ok flag instead of falling through to a default decoder.
Not every pipeline step preserves headers (some tools republish only key and value), so an absent token must be a hard error rather than 'use the default'.
